content.comment_body: Hello everyone! I’m having trouble while developing a fairly large program using [product_name] [product_name] V6.1.16, and I received the following message: "The maximum number of blocks has been reached." Now, I’m unable to add new blocks or connect existing ones. Is there any solution for this besides optimizing my code? My target device is [product_name] [article_no]. Thanks for any help!
Hi, You can optimize your program, or use [product_name] [article_no]. The newer version supports up to 400 blocks!
Thanks for responding! How many blocks does my current [product_name] support?

Hello, The [article_no] version of [product_name] supports 200 blocks. You can check this in [product_name]. Press CTRL-H or, in the tools menu, select hardware and specify your version to view its specs. If you upload your project here, I’m confident we could help optimize your program to use fewer blocks. It’s best to try it yourself first.

Is it possible to use a memory card or something similar to increase the available number of blocks? Just wondering. Meanwhile, I’ll see if I can remove some unnecessary elements from my code. Let me know if you’re able to assist further. Thanks!
Hello, Unfortunately, there’s no way to expand the memory for this device. Memory modules only allow the program to be transferred between units, not to expand block capacity.
